items.stem: What is the period of y = sin 2x (x in degrees)?
items.markingKey: Period of sin x is 360°; sin 2x completes a cycle twice as fast.

items.stem: Explain, using the graph of y = sin x, why sin(180° − x) = sin x.
items.answer: The graph of y = sin x for 0° ≤ x ≤ 180° is symmetrical about x = 90°, so angles x and 180° − x, equally spaced either side of 90°, have the same sine.
items.markingKey: B1 symmetry about x = 90°; B1 x and 180° − x equidistant from 90° [2]

items.stem: Explain why cos x = 2 has no solutions.
items.answer: The range of cos x is −1 ≤ cos x ≤ 1, so it can never equal 2.
items.markingKey: B1 range −1 to 1; B1 2 outside range [2]

items.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = 6 − 7 cos x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π. State the range of f and the value of x at which f has its greatest value.
For the curve y = 1 cos 5x + 3, where x is in degrees, state the amplitude, the period, and the greatest and least values of y.
items.markingKey: B1 amplitude 1; B1 period 72°; B1 greatest 4 and least 2

items.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = 5 − 2 cos x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π. (a) State the range of f. (b) Describe a sequence of transformations that maps y = cos x onto y = f(x).
items.answer: (a) 3 ≤ f(x) ≤ 7 (b) Stretch parallel to the y-axis, factor 2; reflection in the x-axis; translation (0, 5).
items.markingKey: (a) B1 3; B1 7 [2] (b) B1 stretch factor 2 and reflection (or stretch factor −2); B1 translation (0, 5) after [2]

items.stem: What is the amplitude of y = 3 cos x − 1?
items.markingKey: The coefficient of cos x gives the amplitude; −1 is a vertical translation.

items.stem: Explain why tan 45° = 1 using a right-angled triangle.
items.answer: In a right-angled isosceles triangle the two shorter sides are equal and the angles are 45°, so tan 45° = opposite/adjacent = 1.
items.markingKey: B1 isosceles right triangle; B1 equal sides give ratio 1 [2]

items.stem: Lucas says that the period of y = sin 4x is 1440°. Explain the error and state the correct period.
items.answer: Multiplying x by 4 compresses the graph horizontally (stretch factor 1/4), so the period is 360° ÷ 4 = 90°.
items.markingKey: B1 stretch factor 1/4 / cycles faster; B1 90°

items.stem: Samuel says that sin 225° = √2/2. Explain why Samuel is wrong.
items.answer: 225° is in a quadrant where sin is negative, so sin 225° = −√2/2.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies quadrant / sign of sin; B1 sin 225° = −√2/2

items.stem: Mei says that cos 150° = √3/2. Explain why Mei is wrong.
items.answer: 150° is in a quadrant where cos is negative, so cos 150° = −√3/2.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies quadrant / sign of cos; B1 cos 150° = −√3/2

items.stem: What is the range of principal values of cos⁻¹ x?

items.stem: Explain why the domain of sin x must be restricted before an inverse function sin⁻¹ x can be defined.
items.answer: sin x is many-one on ℝ (e.g. sin 0 = sin π), so it has no inverse; on −π/2 ≤ x ≤ π/2 it is one-one, taking each value in [−1, 1] once.
items.markingKey: B1 sin is many-one; B1 restricted interval where one-one [2]

items.stem: Explain why cos⁻¹(−x) = π − cos⁻¹ x for −1 ≤ x ≤ 1.
items.answer: If cos⁻¹ x = θ then cos(π − θ) = −cos θ = −x, and π − θ lies in [0, π], so it is the principal value of cos⁻¹(−x).
items.markingKey: B1 cos(π − θ) = −cos θ; B1 π − θ in principal range [2]

items.stem: Hana says that sin⁻¹(−1/2) = 7π/6, since the sine of this angle is −1/2. Explain why this is not the principal value and give the correct value.

items.markingKey: B1 range −π/2 to π/2; B1 −π/6

items.stem: The equation 2 sin²x = 5 cos x − 1 is to be solved for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°. (a) Show that the equation can be written as a quadratic equation in cos x. (b) Prove the identity (1 − cos x)(1 + cos x) ≡ sin²x. (c) Explain why, in this equation, any value of cos x outside −1 ≤ cos x ≤ 1 is rejected.
items.answer: (a) 2 cos²x + 5 cos x − 3 = 0 (b) Expand: 1 − cos²x = sin²x. (c) The range of cos x is −1 to 1, so such values give no angles.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 sin²x = 1 − cos²x; A1 correct quadratic [2] (b) B1 expands and uses the identity [1] (c) B1 range of cosine [1]

items.answer: sin θ/cos θ + cos θ/sin θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1/(sin θ cos θ).

items.stem: Prove the identity (1 + sin θ)(1 − sin θ) ≡ cos²θ.

items.stem: Prove the identity sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ ≡ sin²θ − cos²θ.
items.answer: sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ = (sin²θ − cos²θ)(sin²θ + cos²θ) = sin²θ − cos²θ.

items.stem: Prove the identity cos θ/(1 − sin θ) − cos θ/(1 + sin θ) ≡ 2 tan θ.
items.answer: Common denominator 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ; numerator cos θ(1 + sin θ) − cos θ(1 − sin θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ; result 2 sin θ cos θ/cos²θ = 2 tan θ.

items.stem: Felix says that cos⁻¹(−1/2) = −π/3. Explain why this is not the principal value and give the correct value.
items.answer: Principal values of cos⁻¹ lie in [0, π], so the answer cannot be negative. cos⁻¹(−1/2) = 2π/3.
items.markingKey: B1 range 0 to π; B1 2π/3

Show that the equation 9 sin²x = −3 cos x + 7 can be written in the form 9 cos²x − 3 cos x − 2 = 0.
items.answer: Replace sin²x by 1 − cos²x: 9 − 9 cos²x = −3 cos x + 7, which rearranges to 9 cos²x − 3 cos x − 2 = 0.
items.markingKey: M1 uses sin²x = 1 − cos²x; A1 rearranges to the given form with correct signs

items.stem: Show that the equation 12 sin²x = −17 cos x + 18 can be written in the form 12 cos²x − 17 cos x + 6 = 0.
items.answer: Replace sin²x by 1 − cos²x: 12 − 12 cos²x = −17 cos x + 18, which rearranges to 12 cos²x − 17 cos x + 6 = 0.
items.markingKey: M1 uses sin²x = 1 − cos²x; A1 rearranges to the given form with correct signs

items.stem: The equation 4 sin²x = 4 cos x + 1 is to be solved for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°. (a) Solve the equation for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°. (b) Explain why, in this equation, any value of cos x outside −1 ≤ cos x ≤ 1 is rejected.
items.answer: (a) 60.0°, 300.0° (b) The range of cos x is −1 to 1, so such values give no angles.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 factorises/solves the quadratic: cos x = 1/2 (cos x = −3/2 rejected); A1 one angle; A1 all angles 60.0°, 300.0° [3] (b) B1 range of cosine [1]

items.stem: Arjun solves cos x = −0.75 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360° and writes x = 138.6° or x = −138.6°. Explain the error and correct it.
items.answer: −138.6° is outside the interval; the second solution is 360° − 138.6° = 221.4°. Solutions 138.6°, 221.4°.
items.markingKey: B1 negative angle outside interval; B1 138.6°, 221.4°

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain why the equation 3 sin x = 4 cos x can be solved by finding tan x. (b) Explain why dividing both sides of sin x cos x = sin x by sin x can lose solutions.
items.answer: (a) cos x = 0 does not give a solution (then sin x = ±1 ≠ 0), so dividing by cos x is safe: tan x = 4/3. (b) Solutions with sin x = 0 (x = 0°, 180°, 360°) are lost; instead factorise: sin x(cos x − 1) = 0.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 cos x ≠ 0 at a solution; B1 tan x = 4/3 [2] (b) B1 sin x may be 0; B1 factorise instead [2]
